scenes.visual: A large schematic Daphne Major fills the frame. Blue shallow-beaked, yellow middle-beaked, and green deep-beaked finches move around it. The title appears briefly above them, then clears. COLOR MAP for both films: shallow beaks blue, middle beaks yellow, deep beaks green; each offspring comes from two parents and tends to resemble them, with some variation; white marks barriers and tests.

scenes.tts: Did the drought reshape these finches, or change which birds remained? On Daphne Major, most medium ground finches died during a severe drought. Researchers had measured their beaks beforehand. The survivors had deeper beaks on average. Watch the population, not one changing bird.
scenes.caption: Did the drought reshape these finches, or change which birds remained? On Daphne Major, most medium ground finches died during a severe drought. Researchers had measured their beaks beforehand. The survivors had deeper beaks on average. Watch the population, not one changing bird.
scenes.visual: Keep the same island and moving flock. A caliper icon records each beak into a schematic three-colour distribution. Dry wind moves across the island. Many bird tokens fade, leaving a survivor distribution shifted toward green. Label every distribution 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Did the drought reshape these finches, or change which birds remained? On Daphne Major, most medium ground finches died during a severe drought. Researchers had measured their beaks beforehand. The survivors had deeper beaks on average. Watch the population, not one changing bird.

scenes.tts: Before the drought, beak depth varied. Beak depth is the height of the beak at its base. Blue birds had shallower beaks, yellow birds had middle beaks, and green birds had deeper beaks. These differences existed before conditions changed. Variation gives the environment something to sort.

scenes.tts: Then drought changed the food. Small, soft seeds became scarce, while large, hard seeds remained. Deeper beaks could crack those hard seeds. Which birds do you predict will contribute more young to the next generation? Follow the colours already on screen.

scenes.visual: Soft seed cartoons shrink and fade while large hard seed cartoons remain. Green deep-beaked birds crack seeds; blue and yellow birds still move but find fewer usable seeds. The three-colour distribution stays visible below. End with the prediction question large and centered.
scenes.narration: Then drought changed the food. Small, soft seeds became scarce, while large, hard seeds remained. Deeper beaks could crack those hard seeds. Which birds do you predict will contribute more young to the next generation? Follow the colours already on screen.

scenes.visual: Hold the prediction question. Birds continue slow searching motions and seeds shift slightly in dry wind. No answer marker appears.

scenes.tts: More green birds survive in this simple picture, but some birds of every colour remain. The groups overlap. A deep beak improves the chance of survival here; it does not guarantee survival. A helpful trait depends on the present environment.
scenes.caption: More green birds survive in this simple picture, but some birds of every colour remain. The groups overlap. A deep beak improves the chance of survival here; it does not guarantee survival. A helpful trait depends on the present environment.
scenes.visual: Reveal a mixed survivor group with more green, while keeping at least one token of every colour. Transform the first schematic distribution into an overlapping survivor distribution. Add 'better chance here' in green and keep 'schematic' visible.
scenes.narration: More green birds survive in this simple picture, but some birds of every colour remain. The groups overlap. A deep beak improves the chance of survival here; it does not guarantee survival. A helpful trait depends on the present environment.

scenes.tts: Survival alone does not finish the mechanism. Beak size is strongly inherited, so parents and young tend to resemble each other. The survivors breed. Their young form another mixed population, now with deeper beaks more common on average. That makes change possible across generations, not within one life.

scenes.visual: Move survivor tokens into parent positions. Pair two parent tokens to produce each small offspring token. Offspring colours tend to resemble the parents' colours but vary; some differ from both parents. Offspring flow into a new schematic distribution with more green than the starting distribution. Keep both distributions aligned for comparison.

scenes.tts: Researchers did not guess which birds survived. Each measured bird had a numbered band before the drought. Later, the team checked which measured birds remained. Comparing the groups connects earlier beak depth with survival. It shows an association, not a promise about every bird. Parents and young provide separate inheritance evidence.

scenes.visual: Zoom to three large carried bird tokens with numbered leg bands and fixed beaks. Move them between 'measured before' and 'checked later' panels. Build two overlapping schematic distributions, then a separate parent-to-young arrow. Label the first 'survival evidence' and the second 'inheritance evidence'.

scenes.tts: This is natural selection. It needs variation, inheritance, and unequal reproductive success. Inherited traits spread when their carriers leave more reproducing offspring. Fitness means that contribution to the next generation. It does not simply mean strength, health, or a long life.

scenes.visual: Transform the two distributions into a single flowing chain: variation, inherited resemblance, unequal offspring. Each term lights as its part moves. Then show the rule centered while parent-to-offspring arrows continue moving behind it.
scenes.narration: This is natural selection. It needs variation, inheritance, and unequal reproductive success. Inherited traits spread when their carriers leave more reproducing offspring. Fitness means that contribution to the next generation. It does not simply mean strength, health, or a long life.

scenes.tts: Mutation supplies new gene versions, and sexual reproduction shuffles them into new combinations. Selection does not produce a trait because organisms need it. It sorts inherited variation that is present, including mutations as they arise. No finch changed its own beak.

scenes.visual: Use labelled gene blocks, never molecular structures. One block changes under 'mutation'; parent blocks recombine under 'sexual reproduction'. Feed the resulting colour variation into the carried population. Place a white lock beside each adult beak to show it stays unchanged.

scenes.tts: The advantage is not permanent. If rainfall and seeds change, selection can change direction. Chance and arrivals from other populations can shift traits too. The drought did not reshape any beak. It changed which birds survived and bred. The next generation carried the population change.
